description: I am a Grade 11 STEM student passionate about science, engineering, and innovation. I have experience in STEM projects, Arduino, electronics, prototyping, and scientific research. I enjoy solving real-world problems, sharing ideas, and working collaboratively. I am looking for motivated, creative teammates with skills in programming, engineering, research, electronics, or design who are eager to learn, innovate, and create meaningful solutions.
summary: We developed an interactive educational browser game designed for kids and teens, following a young astronaut Engineer and a Doctor traveling to Mars to face realistic, high-stakes NASA-inspired challenges that require scientific problem-solving and critical thinking. The game guides players through four critical mission modules covering invisible space radiation and energy shielding, blurry vision microgravity effects (SANS), fitness equipment maintenance, and space agriculture combined with NASA's ECLSS water recycling technology. Featuring a three-heart health system, energy meters, and interactive mini-games like wire-connecting, wrong choices deduct lives and require corrective action while correct choices trigger scientific pop-up explanations and award persistent achievement badges saved via browser storage. Built using pure HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with supplemental visual assistance from design tools, all core concepts, storylines, and logic were entirely created and verified by the team.
details:
Project DetailsWhat it does and how it works (Step-by-Step):Navigation & HUD: Players navigate through three clean pages (Home, Game, and Logbook) linked via a top navigation bar. A persistent Heads-Up Display (HUD) tracks remaining hearts (3 lives), spacecraft energy levels, and unlocked badges. Interplanetary Missions: The player guides the crew through 4 critical scenarios:Mission 1 (Solar Storm & Radiation Defense): Dealing with invisible space radiation and coronal mass ejections, activating radiation shields, managing energy, and solving a wire-connecting mini-game. Mission 2 (Blurry Vision & Microgravity / SANS): Handling microgravity fluid shifts affecting the optic nerve, choosing the correct medical reporting path over risky actions. Mission 3 (Fitness & Equipment): Balancing crew exercise needs and equipment maintenance against energy conservation. Mission 4 (Space Agriculture & Water Recycling): Exploring how astronauts grow food in space and managing dwindling water supplies by implementing NASA’s ECLSS technology to recycle cabin humidity, sweat, and wastewater. Feedback Loop & Pop-ups: After every choice (whether correct or incorrect), an instant pop-up message appears. Correct choices reward the player with an achievement badge and unlock the next phase, while wrong choices deduct a heart (turning grey and lost), explain the scientific consequence, and require corrective mini-game action before re-trying. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Used:Frontend Core: Pure HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (No heavy frameworks or complex build steps, ensuring lightweight and fast execution). Styling & Animation: Custom CSS animations, inline SVG elements, responsive design, and Google Fonts ("Baloo 2"). Data Persistence: Browser localStorage to save collected badges in the Logbook. Benefits and Goals:

Promotes active engagement, scientific accuracy, quick decision-making under pressure, and independent learning through trial, error, and clear explanations. Working Features vs. Future Plans:Working Features: Fully functional multi-page browser game structure, dynamic HUD (hearts & energy meter), 4 complete mission modules with branching choices and pop-up explanations, interactive wire-connecting mini-game, and persistent badge Logbook. Future Plans: Expanding the game with additional deep-space missions, introducing multiplayer collaborative modes, and integrating rich sound effects and voiceovers.
